question: Yesterday you used Claude Code to investigate why your support agent calls escalate_to_human for simple refund requests. You named that session "escalation-audit", and it holds a detailed analysis of lookup_order and process_refund traces. No code or logs have changed since then. How should you continue exactly that prior conversation today?

options.text: Run Claude Code with the -p flag so that the escalation analysis reloads in non-interactive mode.
options.reason: The guide describes -p (--print) as the flag for non-interactive mode, for example in CI. It does not restore a prior named session.

options.text: Start a new session and ask Claude to re-read all the refund traces from the beginning.
options.reason: Nothing has changed, so the prior context is still valid. The guide prefers resumption in this case, and a full re-exploration discards the existing analysis.

options.text: Use fork_session on the newest session so that a fresh branch picks up the escalation analysis.
options.reason: The guide describes fork_session as a way to create independent branches that explore divergent approaches from a shared baseline. It is not the way to continue a specific named conversation.

options.text: Run Claude Code with --resume escalation-audit so that the named prior conversation continues with its analysis intact.
options.reason: The guide names --resume <session-name> as the way to continue a specific prior conversation, and resumption fits because the prior context is still valid.
